identity.production_end_note: LAG-1 (catamarans-lagoon.com/boats/lagoon-42) explicitly labels this design as the manufacturer's 'previous model', distinct from the current 'Lagoon 42 Millennium' refresh referenced on the same page ('You're looking at our previous model. Discover the all-new 42 Millennium'). This confirms the projection below is scoped to the original Lagoon 42 generation -- the same generation named in specs/SEARCH_BENCHMARK.v0.1.md's locked Wave-1 cohort (research/benchmark/SEED_RESEARCH_NOTES.md SEED-18, researched before the Millennium refresh existed) -- and is not conflated with the newer Millennium variant's own (unresearched, unprojected) dimensions, nor with the unrelated, much older c.1990 Van Peteghem/Lauriot-Prevost-designed 'Lagoon 42' built by Jeanneau/TPI Composites/CNB (a different historical generation surfaced only as a Wikipedia lead during REVIEW-amendment research and never used as evidence).

configuration_space_complete_basis: REVIEW-amendment correction. The original wave-1 submission set this flag True on the basis that LAG-1 named only one hull/keel configuration and explicitly marked other genuinely optional equipment (mainsail/Code 0) with '(opt.)' while leaving draft unmarked. Independent review correctly rejected this: absence of a stated second keel/draft option on one product page does not itself prove the factory-relevant configuration space is exhaustive, and general reasoning about how production catamarans of this class are typically built is not admissible proof either. Following the review's instruction, research was extended within the remaining per-design cap to LAG-2 (an independent dealer mirror of the technical-specification table) and LAG-3 (the official RCD-2 'Index G' Owner's Manual -- a comprehensive homologation-adjacent regulatory technical document covering general dimensions, design categories, displacement/loading, rigging, electrical and water systems, and safety). LAG-3 is the strongest and most authoritative document obtained: it explicitly tags several genuinely optional items throughout ('Auxiliary switch (option)', 'Fresh water tank - Port/Starboard (option)') yet states exactly one draught figure ('Draught - Boat fully laden 1,26m') and exactly one L.O.A figure family, with no second keel/draft configuration named or implied anywhere in the ~50-page document. This is materially stronger evidence than a single marketing page, but it remains, in substance, an absence-of-mention: no source obtained -- including LAG-3 -- contains an affirmative statement that the documented configuration is the complete factory-relevant configuration space. Per CLAUDE.md's core guardrail ('Missing/unknown is not evidence that a characteristic is absent') and the review's explicit standard, this is not sufficient to license `configuration_space_complete=True`. The flag is therefore reverted to the conservative `False` default, consistent with how the Oceanis 30.1 pilot and the Bavaria Cruiser 34 in this same wave are both treated despite each having explicitly enumerated multiple named options -- an even stronger evidentiary position than Lagoon 42's single, silently-undifferentiated configuration.
self_authorization_boundary_note: This file is a retained, editable research artifact, not a truth-authorizing one. scripts/search_seed_corpus_wave1.py's shared independent admission oracle (LAGOON_ORACLE) independently re-derives design_id, configuration_space_complete, the exact configuration_id set, and every field's exact value/evidence_refs/scope/direct_or_derived against hardcoded, code-side-only expectations before this file's content is permitted to become Search input, mirroring SLICE-0037 Required Behavior A. The oracle fixes configuration_space_complete=False in both directions: a tampered edit to True fails admission exactly as a tampered edit away from False would for Bavaria/Contessa.

configurations.configuration_basis: The design's single documented hull/keel configuration, independently corroborated across LAG-1 (manufacturer product page), LAG-2 (dealer technical-specification mirror) and LAG-3 (official RCD-2 Owner's Manual). `configuration_evidence_refs` is machine-checked identity evidence; `configuration_basis` remains human-readable audit prose only.

loa_m.scope: REVIEW-amendment correction. LAG-3's '1.2 GENERAL DIMENSIONS' table distinguishes 'L.O.A (Lmax): standard 12,92m' (including removable parts such as bow roller, pulpit and bowsprit, but not the spinnaker pole) from 'L.O.A (Lmax): with Spinnaker pole 13,22m'. The originally retained value (13.22 m, from LAG-1's unqualified 'Length overall' row) is now understood to be this spinnaker-pole-inclusive maximum, not the standard LOA -- the same kind of accessory-extended figure this wave's Oceanis 30.1 and Bavaria Cruiser 34 projections already deliberately exclude in favour of the standard hull-mould dimension. 12.92 m is used here as the literal, direct match for the generic loa_m field; it does not change any Q1/Q2 result (12.92 m still exceeds both the 8-11 m and 9-12 m range upper bounds). Also distinct from the same table's 'Hull length (Lh) 12,79m' row (excluding removable parts entirely), which is not used here either.

beam_m.scope: LAG-1's 'Beam 7,68m', independently corroborated by LAG-2's 'Width 7,68m' and LAG-3's 'Overall width (Bmax) 7,68m' / 'Beam (Bh) 7,68m' (overall catamaran beam across both hulls; design-wide, does not vary by any documented configuration).

draft_max_m.scope: LAG-1's 'Water draft 1,26m', independently corroborated by LAG-2's 'Draught 1,26m' and LAG-3's 'Draught - Boat fully laden 1,26m'. No second draft figure appears in any of the three sources, including LAG-3's comprehensive design-category/displacement tables -- see configuration_space_complete_basis above for why this is nonetheless not treated as proof of configuration-space completeness.
